again.accept: A report came. If you're happy with it, finish the task with “{{finish}}”.
again.answer: The AI carried on and has a question for you. Answer it as before.
again.question: The AI on the task has a question for you. Press this row to open it.
again.received: The front-desk AI has it, and is passing it to the AI on the task.
again.result: The AI on the task sent a report. Press this row to open it.
again.working: The AI has your instructions and is carrying on. A question or report for you moves the task back to “{{section}}”.

guide.closed: The guide has ended. You can show it again from {{settings}} → {{tab}}, under “{{guide}}”.
guide.example:
This is a demo to try the alpacawork flow.
Create an HTML page that shows "Hello" in two fonts, then ask me which one is better.
guide.moreExample: Make one more version so I can compare them.
guide.over: That's the end of the getting-started guide. You can show it again from {{settings}} → {{tab}}, under “{{guide}}”.

say.accept: If you're happy with it, finish the task with this button ({{finish}}). If you'd like something else done next, you can send more instructions instead.
say.anotherRepository: To use another repository, open this, choose “{{create}}”, and pick that repository as its working folder.
say.answer: Choose an option and it goes into the input box. Send it as is to answer. You can also send a different message without choosing one.
say.conversation: Chats with the front-desk AI are disposable. Once they pile up, at a good stopping point, press the line showing its last reply to open the conversation, and clear it with “{{clear}}”. Before that, ask for anything worth keeping to be made a task.
say.direct: The front-desk AI answers short requests right here. Hand it a job, and it becomes a task in the list.
say.label: This label tells the AI which task or project you mean; without it, it goes by the conversation. Send with the right-end button.
say.more: Once you've looked over the report that came, you can keep asking. Try having it make one more version to compare.
say.phone: You can answer questions from your phone when you're away from your desk. The steps are in {{settings}}, under “{{apps}}”.
say.question: Your turn. Press this row to open the question.
say.received: The front-desk AI (the coordinator) has it. It takes a moment to pass it to an AI to work on.
say.result: A report came. Press this row to open it.
say.send: This is the only input box. All your instructions go here.
say.sendAgain: Write what you want done here and send it.
say.stop: To stop the AI, choose “{{stop}}” here, or ask in the input box. You can also ask there to change settings or add a model.
say.unassigned: No AI is on this task yet. Open the row and ask in the input box to start it.
say.working: This is a task. An AI has your instructions and works on it. A question or report for you moves it to “{{section}}”.

pending.long: A new instruction arrived. Waiting for the owner to give a new report estimate.

timeView.axisAbsent: The time view is not saved on this device. It loads when the connection is back.
timeView.help: Scroll sideways to move through time. Zoom with ctrl (⌘) + wheel, a pinch, or two fingers. Double-click the time scale to see everything. Point at a line (tap on a phone) for details. Keys: + − 0 N; press → on a title to read its lines in turn.

welcome.guideOnComputer: The getting-started guide is shown on a wider screen, such as a computer's.
welcome.lead: A place to hand work to a team of AIs.

picture.listed: They're listed. What needs you shows up under “{{section}}”
picture.own: An AI takes each task as its owner, splitting it into subtasks when needed
picture.split: The front-desk AI (the coordinator) turns it into tasks
